hypothesis: The dominant Request244 failure is not merely bad P&L but attempting to trade sparse symbols at states where an order cannot be promptly executed. A causal admission head trained only on pre-decision activity features should identify states where an entry is immediately executable and near-term execution remains available, then improve execution coverage when overlaid on the frozen Request243 controller.

label.immediate_entry_available: first observed positive one-second open within 5 seconds after state_t + 1 second
label.continuation_requirement: at least 3 of 5 future minute anchors have an observed positive one-second open within the same 5-second execution window

features: Request243 causal source/path features only; no future one-second bars, fill labels, exit_reference_open, or policy outcomes

threshold_rule.choose: lowest threshold with tradable precision >=0.80, recall >=0.20 and at least 30 admitted states
threshold_rule.test_block: May11-May20 never used to choose threshold

controller_overlay.rejected_enter: convert ENTER to WAIT and allow the next observed WATCH decision to reconsider
controller_overlay.held_exit: unchanged Request243 HOLD/EXIT sequence; missing exit falls to the precommitted hot_t + 29 minute deadline

forbidden: using future one-second bars as model features
using Request244 P&L to tune the classifier
changing Request243 value heads or HOLD/EXIT logic
opening June or any new holdout
claiming profitability or live readiness from this diagnostic
next_if_pass: Request246 should relearn ENTER versus WAIT action values inside the causally admitted tradable population and evaluate them chronologically under the same one-second execution contract.
next_if_fail: Do not return to action-value tuning. Redesign the observed-liquidity state or execution contract because the model still cannot identify reliably tradable moments.
